The author's motive to highlight the complexities of patriotism and the cost of war is structurally reinforced by the narrative focus on characters navigating moral dilemmas and the consequences of political decisions. By grounding the political thriller in his own experiences as a war correspondent, Franklin uses the characters' internal and external conflicts to mirror the real-world ethical ambiguities of conflict, thereby embedding his thematic intent directly into the plot and character development.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
